```{r setup}
library(explaw)
library(ggplot2)
data(motors, package = "MASS")
```

# Practical Workflow

This vignette demonstrates a complete reliability analysis using `explaw` on the `motors` dataset (40 motors tested at different temperatures, times in hours, right-censored).

## 1. Prepare Data

```{r prepare}
d <- prepare_data(motors, time_col = "time", event_col = "cens", group_col = "temp")
head(d)
```

```{r summarize}
summarize_data(d)
```

## 2. Quick Overview

```{r overview}
indicators_table(d)
```

## 3. Core Estimation

```{r estimation}
# Total exposure time
exposure_time(d)

# Failure rate (MLE) with events & exposure
estimate_lambda(d)

# Exact 95% confidence intervals for lambda and mean lifetime
confidence_interval(d)

# Different confidence level
confidence_interval(d, level = 0.90)
```

## 4. Reliability Indicators

```{r indicators}
# Mean & median lifetime
mean_lifetime(d)
median_lifetime(d)

# Key quantiles (B10, median, B90)
quantile_lifetime(d)

# Custom quantiles
quantile_lifetime(d, p = c(0.01, 0.10, 0.50, 0.90, 0.99))
```

```{r survival-prob}
# Survival & failure probabilities at specific times
survival_prob(d, t = c(1000, 2000, 4000, 8000))
```

```{r expected-failures}
# Expected failures in a fleet of 500 units
expected_failures(d, fleet_size = 500, t = c(1000, 2000, 4000, 8000))
```

## 5. Group Comparison

```{r group-comparison}
compare_groups(d)
```

## 6. Model Checking

```{r check-exp}
# Kolmogorov-Smirnov test
check_exponential(d)
```

```{r qq-plot, fig.cap = "Q-Q plot vs exponential distribution"}
plot_qq(d)
```

## 7. Visualization

```{r plot-survival, fig.cap = "Survival probability curve"}
plot_survival(d)
```

```{r plot-failures, fig.cap = "Expected cumulative failures (fleet of 500)"}
plot_failures(d, fleet_size = 500)
```

```{r plot-groups, fig.cap = "Survival curves by temperature group"}
plot_groups(d)
```

## 8. Customizing Plots

All plots return `ggplot` objects — extend them with standard `ggplot2` syntax:

```{r customize, fig.cap = "Customized survival plot"}
plot_survival(d) +
  labs(title = "Motor Survival (Exponential Fit)",
       subtitle = "Data: motors dataset",
       x = "Operating Time (hours)",
       y = "Reliability R(t)") +
  theme_bw() +
  theme(plot.title = element_text(face = "bold"))
```

## 9. Save Plots

```{r save-plots, eval = FALSE}
p <- plot_survival(d)
ggsave("survival.png", p, width = 6, height = 4, dpi = 300)

p <- plot_groups(d)
ggsave("groups.png", p, width = 7, height = 5, dpi = 300)
```

---

## Complete Script

```r
library(explaw)
data(motors, package = "MASS")

d <- prepare_data(motors, "time", "cens", "temp")

# Report
indicators_table(d)

# Check assumption
check_exponential(d)$conclusion
plot_qq(d)

# Visualize
plot_survival(d)
plot_groups(d)
plot_failures(d, fleet_size = 500)
```

---

## Key Takeaways

| Step | Function | Output |
|------|----------|--------|
| Prepare | `prepare_data()` | Clean `data.frame` with `time`, `event`, `group` |
| Summarize | `summarize_data()` | One-row overview |
| Report | `indicators_table()` | 12-column executive summary |
| Estimate | `estimate_lambda()`, `confidence_interval()` | λ, exposure, exact CIs |
| Indicators | `mean_lifetime()`, `quantile_lifetime()`, `survival_prob()`, `expected_failures()` | Derived metrics |
| Groups | `compare_groups()`, `plot_groups()` | Per-group comparison |
| Diagnose | `check_exponential()`, `plot_qq()` | Goodness-of-fit test & visual |
| Plot | `plot_survival()`, `plot_failures()`, `plot_groups()`, `plot_qq()` | Publication-ready `ggplot` objects |

All functions accept the prepared data frame `d` as first argument. The workflow is linear: prepare → estimate → check → report → visualize.
